author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 수백 마리 · 여름철새 수십 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 해안 소택지, 간척지, 염전, 해안 초습지, 하구 삼각주, 물 고인 논, 갯벌
summary: 봄과 가을에 흔히 지나가는 나그네새이며, 아주 적은 수는 서해안과 일부 섬에서 번식하는 매우 드문 여름철새이다. 해안 소택지, 간척지, 염전, 바닷가 가까운 초습지, 하구 삼각주에 살고, 물 고인 논이나 염전, 갯벌에서 작은 무리를 짓는다. 곤충, 연체동물, 갑각류 등을 주로 먹으며 알은 4~5개쯤 낳는다. 주로 서남부 해안을 지나가며, 국외에서는 알타이–아무르, 히말라야, 일본, 인도, 스리랑카, 미얀마, 말레이반도, 필리핀에 분포한다.

art.subject: Common Redshank (Tringa totanus), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean salt pans and tidal flats in April-May: head and neck pale grey-brown, densely streaked dark, with a short whitish supercilium in front of the eye and a whitish eye-ring; upperparts warm grey-brown with black spots, bars and streaks on the mantle, scapulars and tertials; underparts white, heavily streaked dark brown on the breast and blotched and barred dark on the flanks, cleaner white on the belly and vent; bill orange-red on the basal half and black on the outer half; dark eye; bright orange-red legs.
art.pose: wading in a flooded rice field, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal salt pans and tidal flats in spring, small groups of waders; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing on mud: grey-brown upperparts spotted and barred black, white underparts densely streaked and blotched dark brown, straight bill red on the basal half and black at the tip, bright orange-red legs

adult in flight, seen from above, head, body and tail in line: broad white trailing edge to the inner wing, dark outer primaries, white wedge up the back, finely barred tail, red feet projecting slightly beyond the tail
art.build: Medium-sized, rather stocky Tringa sandpiper, 27.5cm, a little smaller than a feral pigeon; medium-length neck, alert, often bobs the head and body. Bill straight, a little longer than the head, fairly stout at the base. Legs medium-long, bright orange-red, with bare tibia. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight the most distinctive feature is the broad white trailing edge across the secondaries and inner primaries, contrasting with dark outer primaries; a white wedge runs from the rump up the back; the tail is finely barred and the toes project slightly beyond it.
avoid: Do not paint an all-red or all-black bill; only the basal half is red.
Do not give it a long needle-fine bill, very long legs or sooty-black plumage - that is Spotted Redshank (Tringa erythropus), which also lacks the white wing panel.
Do not paint a narrow white wing-bar across the coverts instead of the broad white trailing edge.
Do not paint yellow or greenish legs.
